profile.address: Old Bingham Highway, West Jordan, Salt Lake County, Utah, 84009
profile.reading:
This entry maps to a building within eBay's data center campus in southwestern Salt Lake County, Utah, in the area around the Daybreak master-planned community that straddles South Jordan and West Jordan. eBay selected the Utah site for a data center after weighing a roughly $334 million investment against the state's low earthquake risk, its existing relationship with eBay through a Utah customer-service center, and roughly $27.3 million in state tax incentives tied to job creation. The first building on the campus, delivered in October 2010 through a design-build contract with general contractor Skanska USA Building and mechanical contractor Harris Company, was a Tier IV, fault-tolerant facility of roughly 250,000 square feet across two levels, completed on an accelerated schedule and awarded LEED Gold certification.

eBay expanded the campus in phases afterward. Regional business press covering a September 2013 expansion described a second, connected building drawing most of its roughly 8-megawatt power requirement from on-site Bloom Energy fuel cells running on natural gas, an unusually self-sufficient power arrangement for a data center of that era, with a planned waste-heat-recovery partnership with Ormat to generate additional electricity from the fuel cells' exhaust heat. That expansion employed roughly 60 people on site and was described as the computational backbone supporting transaction processing for eBay's online Marketplace, PayPal, and StubHub. Architectural and engineering-firm project listings for later phases of the campus, referred to in industry material as the "Topaz" campus, with individual buildings identified as SLC01, SLC02, and SLC03, describe subsequent data-hall build-outs inside existing buildings, including one documented at roughly 146,700 square feet with a 10.4-megawatt critical load, again illustrating the scale of construction on this campus without this registry entry being able to tie a specific one of those buildings to this exact mapped footprint.

As with its immediate neighbor in this registry, no eBay-published source gives a street address, building name, or dedicated technical specification for this particular structure. What is documented instead is a broader, well-corroborated history of a large, multi-building, fuel-cell-powered corporate data center campus that eBay has continued to invest in and expand since 2010 to support its core e-commerce and payments businesses.

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 71 (eBay missing-address campaign): found two conflicting, mutually uncorroborated reverse geocoded street candidates for this row and its nearby sibling, neither confirmed by any operator or press source, and declined to guess which if either applies.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] eBay is an American multinational e-commerce company. This specific facility level reading supplements an earlier operator level pass already on file for this operator, which found this appears to be a private, proprietary corporate data center operated internally rather than a marketed colocation or cloud facility, with neither eBays own site nor Wikipedia publishing a specific address. This session made a further attempt. A guessed trade press URL for eBays South Jordan, Utah data center did not resolve, a general aggregator directory for South Jordan hit a page view limit, and the South Jordan, Utah Wikipedia article does not mention eBay or a data center at all. Reverse geocoding this rows own coordinates through a third party service returned a candidate near 6777 West Old Bingham Highway, while the nearby sibling registry row about 250 meters away geocoded to a different street entirely, Crimson View Drive, with no operator or press source confirming either as this specific facilitys actual address. Given these two candidates conflict and neither is independently corroborated, this session declines to apply either.

[2026-09-04 follow-up] This row sits roughly 240 meters from a nearby sibling registry row (osm:way/240724127, "eBay"), both attributed to eBay's South Jordan/West Jordan, UT data center campus, with mutually conflicting, uncorroborated reverse-geocoded street candidates already noted above (this row: Old Bingham Highway; sibling: Crimson View Drive). Independent research confirms eBay operates a large, well-documented, multi-building campus in this immediate area (industry material calls it "Topaz," with buildings referenced as SLC01/SLC02/SLC03), so it is plausible these two OSM points represent two distinct real buildings on the same eBay-owned campus rather than a duplicated map entry for a single building -- but no eBay-published site plan or address list was found to confirm which point, if either, corresponds to which specific building, or whether one OSM way is in fact a duplicate digitization of the same structure. This row's reading and its sibling's reading each describe the same well-corroborated campus history from different angles/phases rather than asserting a distinct address or building identity for either footprint specifically.
